docs.text: Certificate Authorities Org-Tesla Create CA Let’s begin with creating certificate authority to initiate the creation of peer org. Click on Add Certificate Authority. It will show a prompt asking for two options, whether to create a new CA (or) To import CA. Select to create new CA and click on Next. For creating new CA, you will need to fill the following inputs. 1) Display Name – Peer Org CA display name. 2) Domain – Domain to be used with peer endpoints. 3) Organization Name – Name of Peer Org. 4) CA Name – Name of Peer Org CA. 5) Admin Identity Name – Name of Org Admin Identity. 6) Admin Identity Password – Password of Org Admin Identity. Fill in the details and click on Next. It will then verify if CA subdomain is pointed to IP or not. Click on Confirm. Once the CA creation is done, you will receive the success prompt like below. Under the Register Identity tab in CA module, you will see the list of identities registered to the CA which includes a peer, org user and org admin. Org-Netflix Create CA Follow all steps from creating CA till adding peer to create the second peer org.

docs.text: Create Channel: To create a new channel, click on Create channel under the Channels module. Provide the necessary details for channel configuration and click on Add Channel. 1) Ordering Service – Select orderer org from Dropdown. 2) Channel Name – Name of channel to be created. 3) Creator Organization – Select an org which will be used to create the org. 4) Advanced configurations will have fields like max message count, absolute max bytes and preferred max bytes. Those fields are already filled with default values, update it if needed. Once filled all the details, click on Add Channel. You will see the channel creation is done successfully. Now, add peers to the channel. Click on join channel, select peer id and select anchor peer checkbox. Next, click on Join Channel. You will see a prompt saying that peer has joined channel successfully. Under the peers module, select the org from the drop down, click on Joined channels and you will see a prompt saying which channel the peer has joined to. To add second org to the channel, using the first org or the org which you used to create the channel, invite the other org. Click on Add Member. You will see a message saying that the other org has joined the channel. Now, add the peer of second org to the channel.

docs.text: Ordering Service The ordering service module in SutR dashboard will enable users to create orderer org with a defined number of nodes. Click on "Add Ordering Service". Next, you will get a prompt asking to fill the required inputs to create the ordering org. The inputs include below, 1) Ordering org display name 2) Orderer org name 3) No. Of Ordering nodes – As a best practice we can create an ordering service with either 3 or 5 nodes. 4) Channel Name – It is optional for fabric v2.5 5) Domain to be used with ordering endpoints 6) Advanced configurations like max message count, absolute max bytes and preferred max bytes. Explanation of these fields you can find below, Max Message Count: Maximum number of messages allowed in a block before it triggers block creation. Absolute Max Bytes: Hard limit on block size in bytes, triggering block creation when reached. Preferred Max Bytes: Soft limit for an optimal block size in bytes but can exceed if needed up to other limits. Once filled in the inputs, click on Next. It will then verify if the subdomains are pointed to the Ingress IP. So, it is required to point domains before starting to create the network. If you receive all the domains with green tick marks, Click on Confirm. You will see the ordering service started to create. Once it is created, you will see the list below.

docs.text: Organizations (MSP) Under the organizations tab, you will see the peer orgs you’ve created. And it will allow you to download CCP and MSP configuration of the org. CCP (Connection Configuration Profile): -> The CCP file, typically a YAML or JSON file, contains details about the network's structure, including peer and orderer addresses, channels, and certificates, to facilitate client applications connecting to the Fabric network. -> It is used by client applications to identify and connect to specific resources within the Fabric network, such as peers and orderers, belonging to different organizations. MSP (Membership Service Provider): -> MSP configuration defines identity and access control for the organization, including certificates, signing keys, and CA (Certificate Authority) details, which are essential for verifying the legitimacy and roles of network participants. -> MSP ensures that each participant’s identity is authenticated and authorized according to network policies, governing who can participate in transactions and access resources.
docs.title: Organizations (MSP)

Blockchain Use Cases
docs.text: What do businesses actually use these networks for? Think of an enterprise blockchain as a shared record book: several organizations write into the same book, every member keeps an identical copy, and once something is written nobody can quietly change or erase it. Five prominent enterprise use cases explained in plain language for a non-technical audience.

docs.title: 1. Supply Chain Traceability
docs.text: Every handoff is recorded on the shared ledger the moment it happens. Anyone with permission can follow a product's entire journey in seconds. Recalls become fast and precise: only the affected batch is pulled.

docs.title: 2. Trade Finance
docs.text: Buyer, seller and both of their banks work from one shared record of the deal. Letters of credit that took about ten days of paperwork can complete in about a day, and a document registered once cannot be quietly reused.

docs.title: 3. Healthcare & Pharmaceuticals
docs.text: Each pack of medicine gets a digital identity and every handoff is recorded. A counterfeit pack has no recorded history, so it stands out immediately. Patient records are shared only with consent.

docs.title: 4. Digital Identity & KYC
docs.text: A trusted member of the network verifies your identity once and records a tamper-proof confirmation. Other members rely on that proof instantly - Know Your Customer checks without repeated paperwork.

docs.title: 5. Tokenization of Real-World Assets
docs.text: An asset such as an office building or a bond is represented on the ledger as thousands of digital tokens, each a small share of ownership. Trades settle in minutes and the ledger is the single record of who owns what.

docs.title: Where SutR Fits In
docs.text: Every use case runs on a permissioned blockchain such as Hyperledger Fabric. The organizations, peers, ordering service and channels you create with the SutR Dashboard are the building blocks of these networks.

docs.title: MST Proof-Anchoring
docs.text: MST proof-anchoring lets a channel record a tamper-evident proof of each of its transactions onto an external EVM chain (the MST chain), and then write a short anchor status back onto the Fabric ledger. An independent, publicly verifiable timestamp for Fabric activity without exposing any private data - only a one-way commitment (a hash) ever leaves the channel. Opt-in and off by default.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: Capture: as blocks commit the peer computes a commitment hash for each in-scope transaction and stores it in a durable outbox. Anchor: a relayer submits the commitment to the MSTAnchor smart contract on the EVM MST chain. Write-back: the peer records an anchor status on the Fabric ledger through the mstscc system chaincode.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text: All peers and orderers run the MST-enabled binary, mstscc enabled in core.yaml, NodeOUs enabled on every MSP, an EVM MST JSON-RPC endpoint, a deployed MSTAnchor contract per channel, a funded relayer account, the relayer wallet authorized with setRelayer. Run anchoring on a small designated set of peers.

docs.title: Enabling anchoring from the dashboard
docs.text: When creating a channel, expand Advanced Configurations and tick Enable MST Anchoring if the channel should anchor its transactions. The form fields: RPC Endpoint (JSON-RPC URL of the MST EVM node), Chain ID, Capture Mode opt-in or all, Batch Strategy individual or merkle, Confirmations reorg guard, Cadence Mode per-tx batch interval cron, Include Chaincodes, Exclude Chaincodes. The dashboard applies these settings as part of the new channel's configuration - the equivalent of Step 3. Run the preflight check afterwards.

docs.title: Step 1 - Deploy the MSTAnchor contract
docs.text: Deploy one MSTAnchor contract for the channel, transparent upgradeable proxy recommended. peer mst relayer add authorizes each anchoring peer's relayer wallet. Record the contract address and chain id.

docs.title: Step 2 - Configure the peer (core.yaml)
docs.text: Enable the mst section: enabled, channels, evm.rpcURL, evm.minBalanceGwei, writeback mspID certPath keyPath (peer-role node identity), metricsAddr. Also peer.gateway.enabled, peer.discovery.enabled and chaincode.system.mstscc enable. Keep the relayer EVM private key out of files.

docs.title: Step 3 - Enable anchoring on the channel
docs.text: Enable the V2_5_MSTANCHOR capability, add the Application.MSTAnchor value (Enabled, ContractAddress, ChainID, CaptureMode, BatchStrategy, Confirmations, CadenceMode) and widen each org's Writers policy to include the peer role. Apply as a normal channel configuration update.

docs.title: Step 4 - Run the preflight check
docs.text: peer mst preflight validates the channel config against the live chain: enabled, rpc endpoint, chain id, contract, nodeous, writers. Any FAIL line tells you exactly what to fix.

docs.title: Step 5 - Confirm anchoring is working
docs.text: Submit a transaction then peer mst status shows fabric tx id, anchor ref, status CONFIRMED, recorded at. Also peer mst count, peer mst list, peer mst is-anchored.

docs.title: Reading an anchor record
docs.text: Fields: fabric_tx_id, anchor_ref (EVM transaction hash pointer), status CONFIRMED, recorded_at. The ledger record is an attestation plus a pointer, not a proof - use peer mst verify for certainty.

docs.title: Verifying a transaction end-to-end
docs.text: peer mst verify recomputes the commitment from the ledger and compares it against the on-chain anchor. Exit code 0 = MATCH. Verification reads the anchor by transaction id so it succeeds even if the anchor_ref pointer is missing.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Unknown Application ConfigValue name MSTAnchor means stock configtxlator. FORBIDDEN Writers means the peer role is missing from the Writers policy. Anchors on-chain but no ledger status: NodeOUs missing or client cert used for write-back. INVALID_CHAINCODE: old peer binary. MVCC_READ_CONFLICT warning is benign. anchor ref zeros does not affect verification.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text: Peer-local core.yaml mst section: enabled, channels, evm.rpcURL, evm.minBalanceGwei, writeback, outboxPath, metricsAddr. Channel-governed configtx.yaml Application.MSTAnchor: Enabled, ContractAddress, ChainID, CaptureMode, IncludeChaincodes, ExcludeChaincodes, BatchStrategy, Confirmations, CadenceMode.

docs.title: Command reference (peer mst)
docs.text: peer mst preflight, status, is-anchored, list, count, verify, channel-config, onchain, relayer add remove, pipeline. Add -C channel and where relevant --peerAddresses or --rpc.
